_transcription: PAGE MAP: the booklet is 15 rendered pages (idx 0-14 = printed folios 1-15), every one accounted for. idx 0 = bilingual cover (Series AABB2/4, SET-1, Q.P. Code 57/4/1, BIOLOGY (Theory), 2 hours, 35 marks, 15 printed pages, 13 questions). ENGLISH = the EVEN indices 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 (folios 3-15). HINDI = the ODD indices 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. The tops of all seven odd indices open in Hindi (idx 1 Hindi instructions and Q1-4, idx 3 Hindi Q5, idx 5 Hindi Q6(b), idx 7 Hindi Q8, idx 9 Hindi Section C / Q13(a), idx 11 Hindi Q13(b) passage, idx 13 Hindi Q13(b) (iii)-(v)), so no English overflow onto an odd page and no parity inversion; idx 14 (the last page) is English, carrying Q13(b) (iii)-(v). The paper is born-digital, but every row was read off the full-size page by vision. No decimal numbers appear anywhere, so the raised-dot question does not arise. Structure as printed: Section A Q1-6 @2, Section B Q7-12 @3, Section C Q13 case-based @5 = 35. Instruction (vii) says internal choices exist but gives no count; the roster was built from the scheme's four bare ORs (text layer: 4 'OR' tokens, all bare lines) and each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper: Q2, Q6, Q7 and Q13 (four alternatives). Q11 prints (a) and (b) with NO OR between them and the scheme marks both (1+1+1 = 3), so Q11 is one row; Q12 likewise. Q13(a) is a case study (a Bt-cotton vs non-Bt-cotton farm trial and its bar graph) with three sub-parts, one row each, carrying the scheme's split 3/1/1. Its OR, Q13(b), replaces the WHOLE case study with a DIFFERENT case study (a pBR322 passage and map, sub-parts (i)-(v), printed 5x1=5), so it is ONE row Q13b, alternative to Q13ai, with its own passage in context and its own setId (CS2), the shape of 2022 57/2/1 Q13b and 57/3/1 Q13b. The generic lead-in 'Answer the following questions :' (Q13(a)) is an instruction, not passage, and is left out of context. Quotes straightened (Q1 prints curly double quotes; Q12, Q13(b)(i) and (iv) curly single quotes), scientific names plain (Trichoderma, Bacillus thuringiensis are printed italic). Kept as printed: Q2(b) 'belonging to group of viruses', Q5 'belonging to same genus', 'with the same number as', Q7(b) 'relate experimentally, the stability', Q13(b) passage 'for desired results engineered', Q13(b)(iv) 'ori' gene. One question asks the student to produce a drawing of sorts (Q10, a storyboard or flowchart), so one _drawFigure. Nothing on this paper examines content the rationalised NCERT removed: Q5 (mutualism) is Population Interactions and Q6 is Population Growth, both live, so no _outOfSyllabus.

questions.stem: Explain, giving two reasons, how immune response by "vaccine" is different from that by "antitoxin" in humans.
Mention the common bacterium found in the anaerobic sludge during sewage treatment and also in the rumen of cattle. How is this bacterium commercially useful ?
Name the effective biocontrol agents of several plant pathogens belonging to group of viruses. Also write about the ways they support the environment.
Some of the microbes used as biofertilizers are prokaryotes. Name the taxonomic group they come under. With the help of an example, mention how they act as biofertilizers.

questions._flag: Two-subtopic question: the plant half (Trichoderma as a biocontrol agent of plant pathogens) is Microbes as Biocontrol Agents, the human half (cyclosporin A, an immunosuppressant) is Microbes in Industrial Products. Filed on the first, as the stem leads with plants' pathogens in the scheme's own order.
questions.stem: Different species belonging to genus Trichoderma are useful to humans as well as to plants. Justify their roles by giving one instance of each.

The figures given below show the results of a lab experiment in which two microbial species A and B belonging to same genus were grown in three petri dishes having same culture medium. In Petri dish-I, Species-A was grown alone for 8 weeks. In Petri dish-II, Species-B was grown alone for 8 weeks. In Petri dish-III, both the species were grown together with the same number as Petri dish-I and Petri dish-II for 8 weeks.
What conclusion will you draw from the graphs in terms of impact of interaction on growth ? Explain, giving reason.
questions._figure: REQUIRED:three side-by-side graphs of No. of individuals (y, 0 to 200) against Time (in weeks) (x, 0 to 8), titled Petri dish-I 'Sp. A grown alone', Petri dish-II 'Sp. B grown alone' and Petri dish-III 'Sp. A and B grown together'; Sp. A is drawn as a dashed curve and Sp. B as a solid curve, each rising from near 20 and levelling off. The level at which each species levels off alone versus together decides the conclusion the question asks for, so those heights are withheld here. Page idx 4.

questions.stem:
The graphs given below, A and B, represent population of elephants in two different National Parks (a hypothetical situation) at different times.
Study the graphs and comment upon the pattern of growth observed. Mention the possible reason for such patterns seen in nature.
questions._figure: REQUIRED:two graphs of Elephant population (y) against Year (x): graph A with the y axis marked 0, 2000, 4000, 6000, 7000 and the x axis 1900 to 1980; graph B with the y axis marked 0 to 2000 in steps of 500 and the x axis 1960 to 2010. The shape of each curve is exactly the growth pattern the question asks the student to name, so it is withheld here. Page idx 4.

questions.stem: As per a recent newspaper report, a particular country showed declining population growth rate. According to you, what could be the two most possible reasons for this decline and why ?

questions.subtopic: Species Numbers and Patterns of Biodiversity
questions.stem:
The graph given below shows species-area relationship of a certain region.
(i) Study the graph and explain what it represents.
(ii) After a while, a small area was taken for constructing a road which divided the region into two. Write the impact this construction would have on species richness of the region.
questions._figure: REQUIRED:a single curve of No. of species (y, 0 to 500 in steps of 100) against Area evaluated (in hectares) (x, 0 to 60 in steps of 10), starting at the origin. The shape of the curve is what part (i) asks the student to explain, so it is withheld here. Page idx 6.

questions.stem: How did Dr. David Tilman relate experimentally, the stability of a community and its species richness ? Explain.
What are the consequences of loss of biodiversity in a region ? Explain.

questions._flag: The scheme accepts two routes ('//'): Bt spores sprayed on plants (Brassica, fruit trees), which is NCERT's biocontrol section, OR Bt toxin genes put into crops (Bt cotton, Bt rice and so on), which is Biotechnological Applications in Agriculture. Filed on the biocontrol subtopic because the stem frames it as Integrated Pest Management.
questions.stem: Bacillus thuringiensis plays an important role in Integrated Pest Management strategy. Explain how. Name any two crops that are protected efficiently from pests.

questions._drawFigure: a flowchart (or storyboard) of the production of human insulin by r-DNA technology: DNA sequences for chains A and B prepared, introduced into plasmids of E. coli, chains A and B produced separately, extracted, and combined by creating disulphide bonds to form human insulin, each step a box joined by downward arrows. A text flowchart: NCERT prints no figure for it, so there may be no book figure to attach.
questions.stem: With the help of a storyboard or a flowchart only, explain all the stages of how human insulin is produced through r-DNA technology.

(a) Explain the roles of (i) primary, and (ii) secondary lymphoid organs that are responsible for developing defence to combat the action of pathogens/foreign antigens which enter our body.
(b) Doctors generally advise not to undergo surgery of tonsils. Why ?

questions._flag: The award note is printed under part (a), so it covers part (a)'s 1 mark of the 3, not part (b). The scheme accepts both 'Real Time-Polymerase Chain Reaction' and 'Reverse Transcriptase- Polymerase Chain Reaction' for (a); the RT in the COVID test is reverse transcription, which is presumably why the mark was given for any attempt.
questions.stem:
Causative agents of HIV-AIDS and COVID-19 belong to the same group of viruses. To diagnose and amplify the genetic material for further study of COVID-19 virus, 'RT-PCR' test is carried out.
(a) What does 'RT-PCR' stand for ?
(b) Explain the various steps of PCR technique.

questions.context: There are two different farm lands, one where Bt-cotton crop was cultivated and the other where non Bt-cotton crop (indigenous) was cultivated. Farmers responsible for this experimental cultivation were free to use the farming practices of their choice. During the cultivation period, the data was collected with respect to the amount of pesticide used, water required for irrigation and at harvesting time, the crop productivity. Based on the data collected, a bar graph was plotted which is shown below.
questions.stem: Write your interpretation, with reason, on the basis of the three parameters plotted in the graph.
questions._figure: REQUIRED:a bar graph of Number/Litres (y, 0 to 120 in steps of 20) for three groups along an x axis titled Inputs: Crop productivity (Tonnes/Ha), Pesticide (Litres/Ha) and Irrigation (Litres/Ha), with two bars per group keyed Non-Bt average (a crazed, cobblestone pattern) and Bt average (a square grid). The bar heights, and so which crop is higher on each parameter, are what the question asks the student to interpret, so they are withheld here. Page idx 10.

questions._flag: The scheme numbers this part's answers (i), (ii), (iii), (iii), (iv): a numbering slip, its second (iii) answers the paper's (iv) and its (iv) answers (v). The scheme's (v) answer 'No' follows the printed map, which draws Hind III outside both resistance genes; in the real pBR322 sequence the Hind III site lies in the promoter of tetR, a nuance above the syllabus that the solution does not raise.
questions.context: Gene of interest/alien gene is introduced by a cloning vector into a host cell to bring about a desired phenotypic expression in a host cell. The cloning vectors used are plasmid and bacteriophages. Biotechnologists in their labs, for desired results engineered specialised cloning vectors. One such vector is pBR322. Study the diagram carefully and answer the questions that follow.
questions.stem:
(i) What do 'EcoR I', 'BamH I' and 'Hind III' represent ? State their functions.
(ii) Identify the gene you would select for the role of a selectable marker in pBR322. Explain why.
(iii) Write the property/characteristic of plasmid and bacteriophage that makes them efficient cloning vectors.
(iv) Biotechnologists always insert 'ori' gene in their engineered cloning vector. Justify the statement.
(v) Will the experiment be successful if the alien DNA is ligated at Hind III restriction site ? Give reason in support of your answer.
questions._figure: REQUIRED:the NCERT map of the plasmid pBR322: a double ring labelled pBR322 with the regions ampR, tetR, ori and rop marked inside it, and restriction sites labelled round the outside: EcoR I, Cla I and Hind III at the top, Pvu I and Pst I at the upper left, BamH I at the upper right, Sal I at the right and Pvu II at the bottom. Which gene region each site falls in, and in particular where Hind III sits relative to ampR and tetR, decides parts (ii) and (v), so the site-to-gene placement is withheld here. Page idx 12.
